source: GeoNames CC BY 4.0 contemporary GeoNames IDs and coordinates; historical municipal, government, academic, UNESCO, parliamentary, and contemporary journalism linked per period
selection: 25 distinct modern African capital or government-seat settlements not present in batches 01–16. City names, urban lifecycle, sovereignty, and city rank are independent.
coordinateConvention: Modern GeoNames WGS84 EPSG:4326 representative city points; not historical borders, village geometries or relocations.
countryCodeSemantics: sourceCountryCode and featureCode describe present-day GeoNames identities and never historical state allegiance or historical rank.
coverageNote: A-class 1801 or modern-city baseline is only a provisional map editorial selection; it does not assert no historical renamings or attested contemporaneous Korean/English spellings. Exact legal dates are used only where independently documented.
reviewMethod: Use existing staged place identity policy, separate city and historic predecessor, classify A/B/C, record documentary name transitions, generate period choices, validate without overwriting older files.
qualityNotes: 25 GeoNames IDs were checked against all 113 records from batches 01–16. Names, identity, source provenance and exact dates must remain separate.
Rutana GeoNames ID 433635 was explicitly rejected as a false match for Gitega; correct Gitega ID 426272 is a PPLC, whereas Bujumbura ID 425378 is now PPLA.
Bujumbura old Usumbura until 1962; Gitega new German administrative town in 1912. Relocation of Burundi's capital is not a rename.
Addis Ababa modern settlement 1887 per mayor's office; Djibouti 1888 per interior ministry; Windhoek 1890-10-18 per city council.
Windhoek German Windhuk spelling standard 1903-05-14; official form Windhoek restored in 1918. South African military occupation in 1915 alone is not a naming trigger.
Harare Fort Salisbury/Salisbury transitions are separated from officially documented Salisbury to Harare change 1982-04-18.
Gaborone: 1964 planned administrative city, name Gaberones to Gaborone in 1969 (not inferred exact day), distinct from historic Tlokweng and Government Camp.
Maputo: law decree 10/76 issued 1976-03-13 names capital Maputo, effective retroactively 1976-02-05; public announcement 1976-02-03 separately recognized.
Port Louis: municipal annual report explicitly documents Port Nord Ouest in 1801, Port Napoléon from 1803, Port Louis restored in 1810.
Victoria Seychelles: former L'Établissement du Roi renamed Victoria in 1841 per Seychelles National Museum, not during 1811 military conquest.
Antananarivo: Tananarive French administrative label and 1976 reversal recorded at year granularity, avoiding false exact legal day.
Khartoum 1885–1898 destruction/urban decline and nearby Omdurman require a separate verified urban eligibility audit; no unsourced active intervals added.
A-class city timelines are provisional coverage and require source-by-era review before claiming fully verified historical continuity.
No inference of historic national affiliation from GeoNames country code; no urban rank, historical population, tile or runtime release.
No changes to 1–16 staged batches, main, app or release manifest.
Lilongwe source point corrected to latest GeoNames PPLC 927967 (-13.966919, 33.787247); earlier non-GeoNames representative point was rejected.

nameSelectionNotes: 선택된 시대별 한국어·영어·원어명만 names[]에 수록하고 비선택 별명·약칭·추정 번역을 등록하지 않는다.
현행 GeoNames 좌표·국가코드·수도코드로 역사적 국경, 도시등급, 옛 면적을 유추하지 않는다.
도시의 표시 유효기간, 지명 변천, 국가별 시점 영토는 각각 독립적인 조사 대상으로 처리한다.
